name: The Amauris Vienna
positioning: Boutique hotel in a historic palais on Vienna's Ringstrasse, between the State Opera and the Musikverein, with marble interiors and art from the owning family's collection
best_for: Art and design lovers who want a curated room concept and a family art collection
Classical music fans who want to stay between the State Opera and the Musikverein

facts.text: The interiors combine high stucco ceilings with high-quality marble and fine woods.
Conde Nast Traveler describes the hotel as an intimate palais built in 1860 on the Ringstrasse.
The building once housed a bank, and the Opera suite was the manager's office.
The hotel has a turn-of-the-century cast-iron elevator.
The duplex Grand Maisonette suites have freestanding bathtubs.
The Loft suite looks onto St. Charles Church.
Bathrooms feature Acqua di Parma toiletries.
The spa has treatment rooms, a fitness center with Technogym equipment, a sauna and a steam bath.
The hotel is dog-friendly and welcomes dogs.
The hotel is named after the butterfly genus Amauris, which includes the monarch butterfly.
At Glasswing, chef Alexandru Simon centers seasonal tasting menus on ingredients largely sourced from local farmers and producers.

highlights.text: The hotel is on the historic Ringstrasse between the Vienna State Opera and the Musikverein.
Each room features a book, a Viennese work of art, an object from nature, a board game and a selected design piece.
Croatian designer Nikola Arambašić used more than 160 tons of marble in the interiors.
The interiors display works of art from the host family's private collection.
The Opera suite has a Murano chandelier, a balcony and original stucco reliefs.

considerations.text: The pool is a wellness pool with massage jets inside the spa.
WhataHotel notes the limited property size typical of boutique hotels.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the exclusive positioning.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: The Amauris Vienna review
